scope: Corollary 7.1 of the manuscript “Hilbert’s tenth problem over the rational numbers” (preprints/Hilberts-tenth-problem-over-the-rational-numbers-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 004 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f79236c22b981fe6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 56. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: With the usual effective coding, let H10(Q) be the set of integral polynomials having a rational zero, with the number of variables part of the input. Then H10(Q) has Turing degree 0′, the degree of the halting problem. The same is true for each of the following restricted input problems: (i) rational solvability for integral polynomials of total degree at most four; (ii) given a nonempty finite list q1, . . . , qs ∈ Z[X1, . . . , XN ], each of total degree at most two, whether Ps i=1 q2 i has a zero in QN . No bound is imposed on the number of variables, the number of summands in (ii), or the coefficient heights.
